slides.label: Differential Geometry via Forms
slides.notes: Open this capstone by naming the shift in viewpoint. Earlier chapters built forms as measurement devices; this chapter uses them as a full differential-geometry operating system. A coframe measures tangent directions, connection forms record how the frame turns, curvature forms record failed closure around infinitesimal loops, and Gauss-Bonnet turns the local curvature meter into a global topological count.

slides.label: Coframes Replace Coordinate Grids
slides.notes: Emphasize that the coframe is not a decorative choice of notation. It is a local ruler system that may be better adapted to the geometry than coordinates. The duality theta i of e j equals delta i j says that each one-form extracts one frame component. Once the metric is written in the coframe, later structure equations can track geometry without constantly returning to coordinate partial derivatives.

slides.label: Connection 1-Forms Measure Turning
slides.notes: This slide is the hinge between frames and curvature. A frame can move along a curve or across a surface, and the connection forms are the instruments that report the infinitesimal rotation of one frame vector into another. In an orthonormal frame the matrix is skew, so the diagonal does not measure stretching; the off-diagonal one-forms measure rotation between axes.

slides.label: Cartan's Structural Equations
slides.notes: Present the structural equations as a workflow rather than a memorized pair. The first equation says whether the chosen coframe closes up without torsion. The second equation takes the connection one-forms and differentiates them, then corrects by the connection wedged with itself. That correction term is what lets the formula remain geometric instead of merely coordinate-wise.

slides.label: Surface Equations Expose Compatibility
slides.notes: Here the abstract Cartan equations become the classical surface equations. Setting the normal coform to zero restricts the ambient moving frame to the surface. The six resulting equations separate three jobs: metric compatibility in the tangent coframe, symmetry of the shape operator, and the Gauss-Codazzi compatibility that allows a first and second fundamental form to come from an actual surface.

slides.label: Curvature Forms Are Tensor Entries
slides.notes: Make the tensor map concrete. A curvature two-form is not an extra object added after the Riemann tensor; it is the exterior-calculus packaging of the same components. Expanding Omega i j against theta k wedge theta l reads the Riemann tensor entries. On a two-dimensional oriented surface, the single curvature form Omega one two is simply K times the area form.

slides.label: Gauss-Bonnet Is Curvature Accounting
slides.notes: Connect the chapter back to the visual meaning of integration. Curvature forms give local signed area measurements of bending. Gauss-Bonnet says that after adding boundary turning and corner angles, the normalized total equals the Euler characteristic. For a closed sphere the check is particularly clean: total curvature four pi equals two pi times Euler characteristic two.

slides.label: The Same Pipeline Reads Spacetime
slides.notes: Use Schwarzschild as the stress test for the method. Nothing in the Cartan workflow requires a surface in Euclidean three-space. Choose an orthonormal coframe for the Lorentz metric, solve the connection forms from the first structure equation, then compute curvature forms from the second. The plotted light cone and free-fall curve remind students that the forms still measure geometry, now with time in the frame.

slides.label: Capstone Synthesis
slides.notes: Close by asking students to audit every formula by type. What object is being measured, what form performs the measurement, and what invariant should survive a change of frame or coordinates? The chapter's answer is that exterior calculus does not merely shorten tensor notation. It aligns local measurements, compatibility equations, curvature, and global theorems in one visual language.
